findings.title: History cleanup resets the adguard alert before its 15-minute `for` completes
findings.body: The implementation assumes `failedJobsHistoryLimit >= threshold` is sufficient. It is not once the rule counts only recovered failures. `adguard-rewrite-reconciler` runs every 600s with limit 2 and a 120s deadline. After F1/S1/F2/S2, the count reaches 2 and becomes pending; when F3 fails at most about 720s later, the CronJob controller deletes F1 to retain only two failed Jobs, leaving F2 recovered and F3 unresolved—count 1—before the 900s `for` completes. This repeats indefinitely, so the feature's worst documented case remains silent. Kubernetes explicitly retains only the configured number of failed Jobs and deletes the oldest excess Jobs ([controller implementation](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L651-L710)). L7 cannot expose this because it holds exactly two recovered failures for the whole replay and never models F3 or controller cleanup.
findings.recommendation: Make retention cover the pending interval—safest is `failedJobsHistoryLimit >= threshold + 1` for in-scope CronJobs, raising adguard and digest to at least 3. Add a lifecycle replay containing F1/S1/F2/S2 followed by F3 and deletion of F1; mutation back to limit 2 must fail.
